#2416. Florian Wirtz reveals Germany's relentless attacking mentality after Netherlands thrashing

Germany rounded off their 2026 international calendar in emphatic fashion on Monday evening, dismantling the Netherlands at Olympiastadion to secure the top spot in their Nations League group.

Derry Scherhant's superb first-half opener set the hosts on their way before a devastating second-half display saw Florian Wirtz score twice, with Nico Schlotterbeck and Brajan Gruda also getting on the scoresheet.

Speaking to ARD after his 50th international appearance, Wirtz touched on the attacking mentality in the second half, revealing that Germany had no intention of sitting back and protecting their advantage.

“I think we want to stand for playing attacking football,” said the Liverpool midfielder. "We always want to score goals and dominate our opponents.

“We wanted to keep pressing forward and score more goals. And I think we did that perfectly.”

The 23-year-old also admitted that Germany had enjoyed themselves considerably more after the break, having initially struggled to find space against their Dutch opponents.

"Of course, we hope that we can bring the fans a lot of enjoyment. And for us, it was also a lot of fun," Wirtz explained.

"Especially in the second half. The first half still involved quite a lot of hard work and a lot of running.

"In the second half, everything was a little bit easier because we had more space. And that's when it became really enjoyable."

Reflecting on their progress after sealing their third win under Klopp, Wirtz was equally optimistic about what lies ahead.

"It's definitely a fitting way to finish, I'd say, and one that we're very happy with.

"We want to carry on like this next year. That's clear. We want to improve.

"I think we've definitely already taken some good steps forward in our development as a team.

“I'm very proud and happy to be part of this team, and it's really enjoyable.”

#2415. Salvini scherza su Lotito: «Forza Lazio, a prescindere dai presidenti»

Al gazebo della Lega Giovani a Ponte Milvio, il vicepremier ha scambiato battute calcistiche con i presenti.

Matteo Salvini ha scherzato su Lotito durante una visita al gazebo della Lega Giovani a Ponte Milvio, a Roma. Secondo quanto riportato da B-Lab Live!, Parlando di calcio con i ragazzi presenti, il leader della Lega ha salutato un tifoso biancoceleste con un «Forza Lazio» accompagnato da una battuta sui presidenti.

Lo scambio è iniziato durante la foto di gruppo con il nuovo simbolo “Lega – Italia Federale”. Il vicepremier ha chiesto ai presenti di gridare «Forza Milan», tra le risate. Alcuni hanno risposto proponendo invece «Forza Roma».

A quel punto il ministro dei Trasporti ha domandato se ci fosse «qualcuno per Lotito». Dopo i borbottii dei presenti, è stato Salvini a esclamare «Forza Lazio». "Les clubs se professionnalisent de plus en plus et l’écart diminue. Entre la Ligue 2 et le N1, les moyens font qu’en Ligue 2, ils peuvent avoir des tops joueurs, une profondeur de banc, donc sur une saison complète il n’y a pas photo. Mais sur un match, tout peut arriver. Pour moi, le plus gros gap, c’est la Ligue 1 sur le plan de l’intensité et tactiquement.

Si un club de Ligue 2 se présente, je ne dirai pas non, mais je n’ai rien eu de concret pour l’instant. Pour la Ligue 3, non. Je suis dans un endroit où je me sens bien, c’est un choix. Si on prend ce match face à l’ASSE, c’est sûr que ça donne envie de jouer ces rencontres tous les week-ends."

Sauvé par Chico Lamba (à la 50e minute) puis par le poteau (à la 52e), Sainté a concédé l'ouverture du score juste avant l'heure de jeu sur un csc de Nathan Kasia. Les Verts ont profité d'une très brève supériorité numérique (un Haut-Savoyard ayant mis trop de temps à entrer en jeu) pour égaliser à la 68e minute grâce à Ben Old, qui a repris un tir de Thierno Ballo repoussé par le gardien. L'international israélien a ensuite reculé aux côtés de Bernauer au milieu, laissant les jeunes Depalle et Sonko (puis Reynaud) former la paire des milieux offensifs censés organiser le jeu en l'absence de Breum et Boakye... Au retour des vestiaires les Verts sont passés dans un système 3-4-3 avec Le Cardinal dans l'axe de la défense et Reynaud, puis Breum, puis Mendy en milieu offensif en soutien de Ballo et Duffus.

#2397. Caressa sul gol di Frattesi: «Non c’è il tifo dietro»

A Radio Deejay spiega che aveva pensato potesse aver segnato Pio Esposito e cita i problemi tecnici della telecronaca.

Fabio Caressa ha risposto alle critiche per aver urlato meno del previsto durante il gol di Davide Frattesi contro la Francia, quello del momentaneo 2-1. A Deejay Football Club, su Radio Deejay, ha spiegato che nella telecronaca in differita della Nazionale non era sicuro di aver riconosciuto l’autore della rete. Frattesi, centrocampista della Lazio, poteva essere stato confuso con Pio Esposito.

CLICCA QUI E SEGUI LAZIOPRESS.IT ANCHE SU INSTAGRAM

Caressa è tornato sui commenti ricevuti per la diversa enfasi riservata al gol. «Mi dicono che cambio squadra ogni tre giorni per le telecronache», ha detto, introducendo la spiegazione della propria reazione. Le sue parole sono riportate da Webmagazine24.

Il telecronista ha collegato il tono della sua esultanza all’incertezza su chi avesse segnato: «Per esempio, ho fatto la telecronaca in differita della Nazionale e ho urlato un po’ meno al gol di Frattesi perché non ero sicurissimo di averlo beccato, visto che c’era anche Pio».

Caressa ha poi ripreso la domanda che gli è stata rivolta: «Allora tutti mi hanno chiesto: ‘Perché hai urlato meno al gol di Frattesi?’. Perché non ero sicuro, pensavo potesse essere Pio».

#2394. Klopp hails Germany squad after dominant Netherlands win: "This is a very special group"

Germany rounded off 2026 in stunning fashion in Berlin, as they dismantled the Netherlands 5-0 to seal top spot in their Nations League group.

Derry Scherhant opened the scoring shortly before half-time, before a Florian Wirtz brace and goals from Nico Schlotterbeck and Brajan Gruda rounded off a memorable evening.

Following the final whistle, boss Jürgen Klopp reflected on his first six matches in charge, offering an assessment of the expectations that came alongside his summer arrival.

“I had a bit of a feeling in the summer that people thought the new coach, which was me, would have to drink himself into believing the German national team was good,” he said in his post-match interview with ARD.

But he was keen to emphasise just how impressed he has been by the players involved, suggesting that the public perception does not reflect the quality within the German ranks.

"They are wonderful footballers, wonderful, fantastic characters. But the perception from outside isn't like that, because apparently we're constantly chasing something.

"I'm not chasing anything. I'm at the beginning. I don't feel as though I've already been through three tournaments. I simply feel that this is a great team.

“We have pretty good quality, and if we get these highly talented players going, then it won't be much fun playing against us.”

That was most certainly the case for the Netherlands, who saw the game continue to drift out of their sight as Germany romped home in the second half.

“This is a very special group at the moment,” added Klopp. "I know people have heard that a few times before, and our responsibility is to make that visible and keep it visible.

“We can't change the world, but we can show a positive face, and that's what we did today. I think everyone who was here today will go home with a smile on their face and won't question the German national team for at least three or four months.”

The new boss also spoke on the privilege of representing his country after his remarkable club career.

"I've had the great fortune of coaching three big clubs, and I could always identify with those clubs very easily. During my time at each club, there was no other club for me. I loved working there.

“And now I have the great fortune of working for my home country. There's nothing greater, and that's exactly how it felt.”

He was though, adament that Germany cannot get carried away after the result, acknowledging that further improvement will be needed when his side return to action in March.

"Now we have the opportunity to play in the quarter-finals. I've had a look, and there are only really tough opponents in there. I'm already looking forward to it.

“But to say we've suddenly solved all our problems would obviously be nonsense. We've shown something, though, and that was important.”

#2392. Tare: Muriqi scelse la Lazio, rifiutando il PSG e uno stipendio più che doppio

L’ex direttore sportivo racconta l’aereo privato diretto a Parigi e torna sul rendimento dell’attaccante in biancoceleste.

Vedat Muriqi rifiutò il PSG per trasferirsi alla Lazio e rinunciò anche a una proposta superiore a più del doppio dello stipendio. A raccontarlo è Igli Tare, ex direttore sportivo biancoceleste, intervenuto a Sky Calcio Unplugged. Le sue parole, riprese da Chiamarsi Bomber, riguardano sia la scelta dell’attaccante kosovaro sia la sua esperienza a Roma.

CLICCA QUI E SEGUI LAZIOPRESS.IT ANCHE SU INSTAGRAM

Tare riconosce che il centravanti non riuscì a esprimere pienamente il proprio potenziale in biancoceleste. Al tempo stesso ne difende le qualità: «Parliamo di un centravanti fenomenale per il modo di interpretare il gioco e alla Lazio, per vari motivi, non ha dato quello che poteva dare».

Il giudizio dell’ex dirigente distingue dunque il valore attribuito al calciatore dal rendimento avuto alla Lazio. La sua esperienza nella Capitale non rispettò del tutto le aspettative iniziali, soprattutto sul piano realizzativo, pur senza cambiare la valutazione di Tare sulle sue capacità.

Nel racconto di Tare, al momento del trasferimento alla Lazio Muriqi aveva anche la possibilità di raggiungere Parigi. L’ex direttore sportivo descrive così il passaggio decisivo della trattativa: «Aveva un aereo privato con destinazione Parigi al PSG. Ma lui ha rifiutato per venire alla Lazio.»

La scelta del centravanti, secondo la ricostruzione di Tare, fu quindi quella di vestire la maglia biancoceleste anziché partire per il PSG. È il retroscena con cui l’ex dirigente torna su un’operazione fortemente voluta dal giocatore.

#2391. Les U16 butent sur un Andrézieux valeureux

Après le très large succès de la semaine dernière sur Aurillac (9-0), les U16 de Kevin De Jesus faisaient le plus court déplacement de l'année en se rendant chez les voisns d'Andrézieux, classés en 3ème position, juste derrière les Verts. A l'issue de ce match, les positions sont désormais inversées puisque les Andréziens l'ont emporté 3 à 1 après avoir concédé l'ouverture du score.

Les Verts ont rapidement ouvert le score, dès la 8ème minute, sur un penalty consécutif à une faute sur Lenny Nebout et transformé par Noah Fontaine (photo) (Andrézieux-ASSE : 0-1, 8ème). Andrézieux va égaliser à la 13ème minute, suite à un beau mouvement collectif (Andrézieux-ASSE : 1-1, 13ème). A la demi-heure de jeu, Victor Hamouma écopait d'un carton jaune, puis d'un autre quelques minutes plus tard. Les Verts jouaient donc à 10. Andrézieux profitait de cet avantage numérique pour doubler la mise peu avant le repos, dans le temps additionnel. (45ème+3) (Andrézieux-ASSE : 2-1, 45ème+3).Dès la reprise (50ème), les Andréziens faisaient le break sur coup-de-pied arrêté (Andrézieux-ASSE : 3-1, 50ème). Malgré leurs efforts, les Verts ne parvenaient pas à revenir au score.

La composition : Delgado - R.Fontaine (Moussaoui, 26ème), Ahamadi, Hamouma, Moser - Evaristo, Rochette, N.Fontaine (Nebout, 81ème) - Nebout I.Camara, 60ème), Durin, Giangreco (L.La Rosa, 60ème).

La réaction de Kevin De Jesus : "C'est une belle victoire d'Andrézieux, victoire méritée d'une équipe valeureuse qui a bien joué les coups. Nous n'avons pas réussi à nous créer beaucoup de situations ou d'occasions. Nous devons faire beaucoup mieux, exister plus techniquement, mais également dans le rapport de forces, dans les duels. Les derbys sont toujours difficiles, c'est un contexte particulier face à un adversaire qui a envie de montrer qu'il peut rivaliser."

#2387. Bosz frustrated as Feyenoord hold PSV to 1-1 draw in Eindhoven

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Feyenoord preserved their four-point advantage over champions PSV after coming away with a point from Eindhoven thanks to an improved second-half performance.

PSV dominated the first half as they deployed a close-passing, tiki-taka style to stifle Feyenoord, but only had Guus Til’s well-taken volley after 20 minutes to show for it.

Ten minutes after the break Feyenoord equalised when Anis Hadj Moussa was given too much space to charge down the right flank and bend a shot inside the far post.

The Algerian had a good chance for a second towards the end, while PSV goalkeeper Matej Kovar had to be alert to keep out a header by Nacho Ferri from close range.

“We were by far the better team today and had the better chances,” said PSV coach Peter Bosz. “We started the second half badly and made a mistake, after which Hadj Moussa scored. And even then we could have won it.”

Ajax overtook PSV to close the gap at the top to three points with a hard-fought win at Sparta. Veteran striker Jens Toornstra scored for Sparta on his 500th Eredivisie appearance, but Abdellah Ouazane and Tolu Arokodare, the scorers against Atalanta in midweek, were on target again to claim the win for Ajax.

Twente moved up to fourth place as two late goals by Sondre Ørjasæter and Lucas Vennegoor of Hesselink earned a 2-0 win at AZ Alkmaar, who like Twente and PSV have 20 points.

Fortuna Sittard also snatched the points late on against Excelsior as Rodrigo Guth headed in a corner in injury time to keep the Limburg club in sixth place, two points further back.

At the other end of the table, the return of Adrie Koster as veteran coach brought no relief to Willem II, who crashed to a 6-1 home defeat to Cambuur.

The Tilburgers remain four points behind ADO Den Haag, who were unable to keep up the momentum of last week’s win against PSV as they lost 3-2 at home to Heerenveen.

Telstar lost by the same margin at Go Ahead Eagles, whose striker Søren Tengstedt netted twice in the first half to lead the Eredivisie scoring charts with eight goals.

#2386. Pancaro e la Lazio, a Nepi il premio nel nome di Tommaso Maestrelli

L’ex difensore ha ricordato la vittoria dello scudetto nel 2000 e il rapporto con Massimo Maestrelli, presente alla cerimonia.

Giuseppe Pancaro ha ricevuto il Premio Sport del Lazio Club Nepi T. Secondo quanto riportato da Corriere dello Sport, Maestrelli nella Sala Consiliare del Comune di Nepi. L’ex difensore biancoceleste ha ripercorso la sua esperienza alla Lazio e ha ringraziato il club per il riconoscimento.

CLICCA QUI E SEGUI LAZIOPRESS.IT ANCHE SU INSTAGRAM

Il Lazio Club Nepi Tommaso Maestrelli 1967 ha dedicato la cerimonia a Pancaro, protagonista della storia recente biancoceleste. All’appuntamento era presente Massimo Maestrelli, figlio di Tommaso, l’allenatore del primo scudetto della Lazio e una presenza ormai costante agli incontri del club.

Pancaro ha accolto così il premio: «Per me è un onore essere qui a Nepi oggi con voi. È un grande onore ricevere un premio dal Lazio Club Nepi intitolato a Tommaso Mestrelli, perché sappiamo chi è stato e chi è ancora oggi Tommaso Mestrelli per la Lazio e per i laziali.»

Con la maglia della Lazio, Pancaro ha conquistato, tra gli altri trofei, lo storico scudetto del 2000. Durante l’incontro è tornato sui momenti più significativi della sua carriera nella Capitale e sul rapporto che conserva con il mondo laziale.

#2385. "We had to adapt" – Klopp breaks down tactical approach to stun the Netherlands

Putting the Netherlands to the sword 5-0 in Berlin this evening, Jürgen Klopp was bowled over by his team's ruthless performance which saw them top Nations League Group A2

“It was really extraordinary. The match was exceptionally difficult. Against a really good opponent, you have to find a way,” the DFB head coach said in an interview with ARD.

"We had to adapt, had to change a few things — actually, some big things — and we made those changes, took a lot away from them and then scored some unbelievable goals.

“It was madness. A great football match and a fantastic result. To be able to do that here in Berlin, in the last international match of the year, I wouldn't have dared to wish for that,” he said.

Regarding the national team's tactical approach against the Netherlands this evening, the 59-year-old said his side had to tweak some tactics midway through the game.

"In all the other matches, we were incredibly dominant. Today was intense in a completely different way. Both teams wanted to press high, and neither team did the other any favours.

"Instead, they were playing the ball over each other's heads.We tried to keep things simple. Whenever we could play out quickly, that's what we wanted to do.

"Otherwise, there was no point driving ourselves crazy. I thought we could leave the perfect build-up play against high pressing for another time. We'll do that when we have two weeks.

"So we wanted to play towards Kai [Havertz] and compete for the second balls. When the ball was on the ground, they caused problems with Reijnders operating as a number ten.

"Meanwhile, Malen occupied both centre-backs. They made us run. You have to be braver in those situations. You have to allow a defender to step out."

“Either Jona [Tah] or Schlotterbeck had to step forward into midfield to defend. At that point, we started causing them problems,” Klopp explained with great detail.

Two of Germany's least experienced attackers, Derry Scherhant and Brajan Gruda, were both singled out for praise by Klopp. He felt the duo put in a remarkable shift all night.

"The work they put in, the work they had to do today, was brutal. That's what makes a team in the end, because other players can play football too.

"But it's about what you put into it in terms of commitment and passion. That's what matters in the end. These lads are still surprising themselves."

“Today we showed that we can also be devastating when attacking quickly. That's something we hadn't shown before,” Klopp concluded.

#2382. Sports club members becoming less tolerant of homosexuality

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Acceptance of homosexuality in Dutch sports clubs has declined significantly in the last generation, according to a survey of attitudes by the Mulier Institute.

The organisation found that 66% of people had no objection to a fellow member of a sports club being gay, while in 2008 the figure was 85%.

Just over half (55%) of respondents said they had no problem sharing a shower with a gay team-mate of the same sex, which also represented a drop from 73% in 2008.

The Mulier Institute said the findings reflected a social trend that has also been seen in schools, where the proportion of boys aged between 12 and 16 with a positive view of homosexuality has dropped from 40% to 22% since 2021.

The Dutch Olympic Committee NOC*NSF said the findings were “highly regrettable” and pledged to step up its efforts to make sport more inclusive.

But the John Blankenstein Foundation, which campaigns for LGBT emancipation in sport, said it had noticed declining enthusiasm for its workshops and growing numbers of parents who voiced objections.

Karin Blankenstein, who set up the organisation in 2008, told NOS: “I get the sensitivity around transgender people in sport at the top level, but this is about amateur sport.”

#2378. Kimmich reflects on Germany's resurgence: "That gives us confidence for next year"

Joshua Kimmich is full of optimism as the second international break under Jürgen Klopp draws to a close.

Sealing their second win in the space of a week, Germany rounded off 2026 in emphatic fashion on Monday, beating the Netherlands 5-0 in Berlin.

Derry Scherhant opened the scoring before half-time, before Florian Wirtz, Nico Schlotterbeck and Brajan Gruda rounded off a fantastic evening in the capital.

Speaking to ARD after the final whistle, captain Kimmich reflected on a difficult year for the Nationalelf, which included the third-straight disappointing World Cup campaign and the subsequent appointment of Klopp.

“From the national team's perspective, it's obviously been turbulent, shaped by a very poor World Cup. Now it's something of a fresh start,” the Bayern Munich and Germany midfielder admitted.

"We had the first international break with the split squad, where we already had a good feeling, but still didn't quite know where we stood.

“I think we've now played two very, very good games. You could already see the direction we want to take with our football and how we want to play.”

The 31-year-old was particularly encouraged by the aggressive approach, with the hosts not letting up throughout the second half - something also echoed by Wirtz on the night.

"Of course, we'd hoped that we would win the game today. But above all, it was about the way we want to play football.

"I think you could see over the 90 minutes that we wanted to press high. We won the ball back in a lot of good positions. course, the first two goals were outstanding strikes. They probably don't go in every day."

Despite Germany's eventual dominance, Kimmich acknowledged that the opening period had been far from straightforward, with both sides struggling to establish control.

"I thought the first half was a little unsettled for both teams. Holland probably had the biggest chance with the header.

"But in the second half, it was a really great performance from us."

After the emphatic win, Germany now turn their attention to March's Nations League quarter-finals, with Klopp's side hoping to build on their encouraging finish to 2026.

A late equaliser for Fortuna Sittard in De Kuip proved costly for Feyenoord as PSV and Twente racked up huge victories to move within two points of the Eredivisie leaders.

Twente recorded the biggest win of the weekend with a 9-0 demolition of Excelsior in Rotterdam, with Wout Weghorst scoring four times and Sondre Ørjasaeter notching up five assists.

Excelsior collapsed following the fifth-minute dismissal of Nesto Groen for a reckless high challenge. The home side were 5-0 down at half-time, with Weghorst claiming a hat-trick in the opening 33 minutes.

PSV bagged seven goals in a one-sided encounter with bottom club Willem II, with all the goals coming from different scorers including Ricardo Pepi, who came on in the second half after a six-week absence through injury.

The match between Cambuur Leeuwarden and Go Ahead Eagles was suspended in the 82nd minute after visiting fans threw fireworks onto the pitch.

The clubs agreed with the KNVB not to play the final minutes and allow Cambuur’s 4-0 advantage to stand as the final result.

Go Ahead’s director Jan-Willem van Dop said the club would take action against those responsible: “I am ashamed on behalf a small group of supporters who ruined things for the club and a large hare of the fans in the away end,” he said.

#2373. Dual passports issue continues to plague Dutch-based footballers

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Dutch-born footballers who were called up to play for former colonies such as Suriname and Indonesia are still in limbo over their national status, six months after the “passportgate” crisis first flared up.

Suriname’s parliament passed a law in September enabling players who are selected for the national team to gain citizenship automatically.

But the Dutch immigration service IND said the law passed in Suriname made no difference to the rules on dual nationality in the Netherlands.

“The fact that Surinamese nationality has been obtained by legal means is not enough on its own to qualify for one of the exceptional categories under our law,” a spokesman for the Dutch justice ministry told broadcaster NOS.

The law was intended to settle the question of dual nationality for footballers, which arose last March when NAC Breda challenged the eligibility of Go Ahead Eagles defender Dean James.

James took Indonesian citizenship last year after accepting an invitation to play for the national team, but under Dutch dual nationality rules he was required to give up his original passport.

The Dutch football association KNVB launched an investigation into the employment status of players who were called up by countries such as Suriname, Cape Verde and Indonesia. In the meantime it arranged for Dutch-based players to be given temporary work permits so they could keep playing for their clubs.

Losing Dutch nationality also stripped them of their EU citizenship, meaning they would need to obtain visas and meet stricter criteria, such as an annual salary threshold of €600,000, to be eligible to play in the Eredivisie.

Several players have passed up invitations to join the Surinamese squad because of the uncertainty, including Danilho Doekhi of Lazio, Milan van Ewijk of Coventry City and Jayden Oosterwolde of Fenerbahçe.

National team manager Henk Fraser said it was “inexplicable” that players’ livelihoods were being damaged by their desire to play international football.

“Both countries have to get together and clarify the situation,” he told NOS. “This is a straightforward case of people following their hearts and wanting to play for Suriname, but not knowing where they stand.”

Some players said they felt misled by the Surinamese football association, which told them they were playing for the national team on “sports passports” that allowed them to remain Dutch citizens.

Former Feyenoord winger Jean-Paul Boëtius said he only discovered after he was first called up for Suriname last year that he had inadvertently renounced his Dutch citizenship as a result.

Shortly afterwards he received a letter from the city council in Rotterdam telling him to hand in his Dutch passport, which he had recently renewed, because it was no longer valid.

“I now have a sticker in my Surinamese passport that says I have a residency permit allowing me to live in the Netherlands,” he told NOS. “But that’s only for a year. It’s a very difficult situation. I want to become Dutch again. I was born and brought up here.”

Football is the world’s most famous sport, and it is the sport of choice of a great many sports punters as well. Especially popular in Europe, betting on football can be an incredibly profitable enterprise, so long as you know how to do it.

Getting started on football betting is far from easy, though. This form of gambling requires dedication, investment, and persistence. As you gain experience, your intuition will improve and you will be able to make more correct predictions.

But experience is not the only thing that can help you become a better football punter. In fact, you can substantially improve your betting strategy by simply following some basic football betting tips.

You might find shopping around boring and unhelpful, but you just have to do it when you search sites for football betting. As you know, the higher the odds, the bigger the payout. What you may have missed, however, is that odds are different at each bookmaker. Having said that, shopping around for the best odds is sensible, as it rewards you with bigger payouts.

In this line of thought, sticking to one bookmaker is virtually pointless. Even if the bookie of your choosing offers the best odds for a number of matches, it is highly unlikely that their odds will remain the best for long.

An obvious one, we know. And yet, you will be surprised by the number of football bettors who wager on football, but do not follow the sport. So, why is it important to follow the action closely?

First of all, by watching football matches, you can take part in the most exciting football betting market – the live betting market. What is more important, however, is that following the action provides an invaluable insight into teams and players’ style, condition, and determination – important factors  to consider when placing a bet.

As you watch more and more games, you will improve your analytic abilities. In time, you will be able to make more accurate predictions about the outcome of different matches, which, of course,  will result in placing more winning bets.

As you know, odds are based on the probability of occurrence of a certain outcome; the higher the odds, the more unlikely it is for that outcome to actually occur. But what happens when the odds offered by the bookmaker represent a probability that is lower than the actual probability of an outcome occurring? In such a situation, you can place what is called a value bet.

If you want to become a professional football punter, you should always search for value when betting, as it leads to huge profits

Favoured by beginners in particular, accumulators are a type of football wager which allows you to bet on as many fixtures as you like. Most commonly, you will be asked to choose a match winner, but as the market is diverse, you may be offered a number of other betting options. What makes accumulators an appealing betting market is the huge potential payout – here, you can stake as little as £1 and have the potential to win more than £500,000, depending on the bookmaker and the number of selected fixtures.

If you find accumulators’ payouts too good to be true, you are right. As a matter of fact, there is a reason for the odds to be set so high – actually winning an accumulator bet, especially one which involves a wide selection of matches, is nearly impossible. You see, all you need for your whole wager to lose is one wrong prediction. For example, if you bet on 10 matches and just one of them goes wrong, your entire accumulator is lost.

To make money by betting on football, avoid betting on accumulators – the risk is simply not worth it.

Finally, if you want to be a successful football punter, learn how not to mix emotions with betting. This is easier said than done, though.

Whenever your favourite team plays, you want them to win, regardless of how (im)possible that may be. If you do not learn how to leave emotions out of betting, however, you are highly likely to put money on your favourite team even if they have no chance of winning the match. Conversely, should you base your bets on hard facts and not on emotions, you increase your chances to win.

Our advice – avoid betting on fixtures that involve one of your favourite teams, that is the easiest way to keep emotions at bay.

#2368. Feyenoord facing fireworks fine after 3-0 loss to Internazionale

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Feyenoord are facing a heavy fine from European football authorities after fireworks were let off during their Champions League defeat by Internazionale.

Referee Glenn Nyberg suspended the match for several minutes after flares were fired onto the roof from outside De Kuip stadium, damaging the structure. Police later made two arrests.

“It’s obviously not right and it’ll be another fine,” coach Giovanni van Bronckhorst said wearily after the game, which ended in a comprehensive 3-0 defeat for his team.

One flare landed on the pitch despite the club taking measures such as hanging nets from the gantries to stop objects being thrown from the stands. “They’re letting off fireworks from outside now,” Van Bronckhorst said. “What do you do about that?”

Uefa are likely to hit Feyenoord with a fine and could order the club to close parts of the stadium for their next home matches in the competition, against Porto on November 24 and RB Leipzig on January 27.

The club also have a suspended penalty hanging over them from last October, when they were fined €60,000 after fans let off fireworks during the match against Greek club Panathinaikos.

On the pitch, Feyenoord were undone by a classic display of Italian defending and counter-attacking, as Internazionale sat back after taking an eighth-minute lead through Yann Bisseck.

Francesco Pio Esposito headed in a second early in the second half, just as Feyenoord were pushing for an equaliser, before Piotr Zielinski made sure of the win with a shot from 20 metres.

Captain Luciano Valente said the result was “more than deserved” and the visitors had shown more “quality”.

“This defeat was harder to take than the one against Barcelona,” he told Ziggo Sport. “Because we thought going in that we could get something, but we just weren’t good enough.”

Van Bronckhorst said he was not surprised by the difference in class between the teams. “They scored the first goal out of nothing,” he said. “And Inter know better what the game needs at every stage.

“Their players have a lot of experience, they’ve been in the final twice in the last four years. So we’re at a disadvantage.”

#2364. PSV edged out by sharper Club Brugge in Champions League defeat

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

PSV Eindhoven endured a frustrating night in the Champions League as their defensive frailties were exposed in a 2-1 defeat by Club Brugge.

PSV started full of attacking intent and should have taken an early lead when Ivan Perisic put Sergiño Dest clean through on goal, but the defender’s shot was too close to goalkeeper Yann Sommer.

Instead it was the visitors who took the lead with their first real attack when Nicolo Tresoldi headed in a teasing cross from Joaquin Seys.

PSV equalised early in the second half as an outstanding pass by Sven Mijnans into the path Lutsharel Geertruida allowed the defender to charge to the byline. His pullback found its way to Kodai Sano, whose shot took a deflection off Seys into the net.

But five minutes later PSV were caught out as another razor-sharp pass by Seys released Carlos Forbs in space to net the winner.

The home side refused to give up, but were unable to find a way past Sommer in the closing stages as the Belgian side closed out the win.

Team captain Mauro Junior admitted that PSV had been undone by shortcomings at the back. “We had a lot of opportunities in the first half but we didn’t score,” he told Ziggo Sport.

“We want to attack and score goals, but we weren’ well organised today in defence. We need to keep our heads up and look forward to the next game.”

The result leaves PSV in 24th place, just above the elimination line, ahead of their next match away to Real Madrid on November 24, with four points from their opening four matches.

#2363. Opinion: The morality of football

Yesterday evening, Selecao correspondent Nathan Motz accepted a unique opportunity to appear as a guest on the Moral Maze – a BBC radio broadcast dealing with matters of moral and ethical significance.

Is football a moral force for good? That was the question of the day, and each of the four guests were asked to discuss various aspects of the debate from financial fairplay to club takeovers by foreign entities to racism.

Nathan’s segment was concerned with whether football has transcendent moral value, and what that is exactly. Is there a greater significance to the game we are watching, or is it merely 22 humans kicking a leather ball into a net?

Join Nathan as he elaborates on the most significant takeaways of what was a fascinating discussion on the sport and morality in general.

Football, for some, may be the most poignant reminder of the moral universe in which we live. While debate has raged for centuries regarding the precise origin of moral absolutes and how humans ought to live, it is simply unavoidable to say humanity is often troubled by events surrounding the game we all love so dearly.

In not so distant history, every normal act of human life would have been assigned some degree of moral significance. Every action had inherently moral indicators - for good or for evil. Today, postmodern views of morality dominate. These describe morality as an entirely subjective dimension. In other words, it cannot be pinned down exactly whether behaviors are objectively good or bad. We can only find fault with someone else’s interpretation based on their own unique moral code. Morality is relative to the individual or society.

Yet last night’s dialogue concerning football and human behavior was filled with moral accusations and claims which strongly suggested humans are not content with relativist morality. Indeed, we are at times frightened by and disgusted with what we observe in and around football. Our sense of moral justice is deeply disturbed. But with respect to what exactly?

In responding to the panelist’s questions, I observed a familiar paradigm. Each time I have discussed any aspect of moral behavior, the speculation humans are good or at worst morally neutral animals continually reemerges. This widely accepted presupposition is then followed shortly by disgust at some aspect of human behavior. Almost as if to ask “why are all these good humans behaving so badly?” while ignoring the very real implications of this line of inquiry. A question rendered unanswerable by the insistent a priori assumptions from which it was derived.

If humans are intrinsically beneficent, conscientious, fair, humble, and honest then why is football rife with racism, misogyny, greed, disenfranchisement, lies, cheating, violence, and the hypocrisy to deny the occurrence of any such behaviors except when a rival club is the guilty party? Behaviors which are perpetrated by individual supporters, fanatical groups, club administrations, corporate bodies such as FIFA, political entities, nations, and even the players themselves. No one participating faction is guiltless.

To so blithely sidestep more sufficient explanations for the empirical reality of wickedness in football and in human behavior more generally is not just factually incorrect. It undermines real attempts to understand the root of these behaviors where they might be dealt with more effectively.

To listen to The Moral Maze episode entitled “Football: a moral force for good?” produced by BBC radio and featuring PortuGOAL’s Seleção correspondent Nathan Motz click on this link

Furthermore, in good faith, how successful is a response against heinous evil when those perpetrating it are regarded as behaving in accord with their unique moral ambitions? Humans refuse to accept their indisputably objective moral lacking at a fundamental level. This restricts us from ever doing any more than “stamping out” the alleged impropriety of others – while we ourselves may readily engage in these very same behaviors. Moral relativism cannot account for the moral outrage emanating from all corners of the football world. Is Qatar wrong to perpetrate human rights atrocities or is it allowable because their culture is indifferent? Is hooliganism objectively wrong, or only when someone else’s club is responsible?

The overlooking of our own failings while lashing out at others for theirs is quintessential to the morally fallen nature of humanity itself. Football tells all. There are not good people and bad people. There are only people who both willfully and unintentionally transgress the moral code embedded in each of our hearts. A moral law which can only have ever been given by a moral Lawgiver. Otherwise, it is truly your word against mine as it pertains to the moral validity of all behaviors - even those which may deeply violate your conscience.

Football generates an episodic, semantic, and imagistic description of universal archetypes: good and evil, sacrifice and greed, cruelty and mercy, hero and anti-hero. It speaks to every arc of life’s plotline: tragedy, comedy, victory, defeat, the finite nature of our circumstances. It is one of the preeminent existential dialects alongside religion, visual art, written and spoken language, music, and theatre. Football plucks a primal chord.

As metaphysics have been curtailed to just physics in the modern secular West, football has only elevated our awareness of the often dire moral predicaments of our species. Yet it is clear the moral conversation does not originate on a football pitch. The pitch is but a grand stage upon which moral themes may be observed and critiqued, a mirror held in front of our own soul.

The desire for ultimate purpose, for meaning beyond the material realm, never disappeared in modernity. Arguably, it has only become more desperate as the outcry for ultimate significance comes under more scrutiny and criticism by those who constrain ontological explanations to those accounted for by physics. The severity of the mental health crisis in the West is in no small part explained by the terrifying existential awareness we are cut adrift in an abstract sea of meaningless, hopeless wandering between two oblivions - that before mortal life began and that at mortal life’s end. Let football be one voice which reassures you - there is ultimate meaning and good reasons why football so unsettles our craving for justice.

In a palpable, unavoidable way, football and supporter communities across Europe are encountering moral quandaries. In Portugal, age-old debates between FC Porto and Benfica have routinely been haunted by, in many cases, farcical and cynical hypocrisy. Throughout its history, the FPF has been susceptible to showing partiality to a club, player, or style which ultimately degrades the performance of our beloved Seleção. Deny it all we like, and not one aspect of this reality is changed.

In conclusion, whatever your thoughts or beliefs on the subject of moral significance, its origin, the meaning of life, and how football draws that out, I hope it will be beneficial to examine these matters more deeply. In my zeal, I admit I have not always been prudent to initiate these discussions in a way which respects thoughtful disagreement. It is my hope this effort to bring that discussion to Portuguese football will be well-received and carefully pondered. But I will contentedly listen to those followers who may be genuinely unhappy or unsupportive of this or any other idea about which I write.

The readers of this website and the larger Portuguese football loving world are my people. It is a joy and a responsibility I take seriously whenever I have the opportunity to raise important questions about the Selecao, the game, and our lives in general.

#2362. Les Vertes sont mieux que des Nice Girls

Les Amazones poursuivent leur sans-faute en Arkema Seconde Ligue !Ce samedi, les protégées de Yannick Chandioux ont décroché leur sixième succès consécutif en dominant l'OGC Nice (1-0) au stade Salif-Keïta. Avant cette rencontre, les Stéphanoises occupaient la première place du classement avec 17 points, devant Le Mans et Roubaix, tandis que les Azuréennes pointaient au dixième rang seulement.Pour conserver son fauteuil de leader, le coach ligérien avait reconduit Ithaisa Viñoly dans les cages, derrière une défense Couasnon-Kack-Blanchard-Sierra. Faustine Bataillard et Héloïse Mansuy étaient chargées de l'entrejeu, tandis que la capitaine Sarah Cambot accompagnait Jana Zufankova, Tyler Isgrig et Dona Scannapieco dans le secteur offensif.Et les Vertes ne tardaient pas à prendre les choses en main malgré une première (et la seule) intervention d'Ithaisa Viñoly. D'abord une première tentative de Jana Zufankova dès la 2e minute puis une ouverture du score logique au quart d'heure de jeu: sur un centre parfaitement ajusté de Sarah Cambot, Tyler Isgrig surgissait au second poteau pour placer une tête victorieuse et inscrire son 5e pion de la saison, le 4e enc championnat (1-0, 15e).Les Amazones manquaient même le break dans la foulée lorsque la tentative de Mansuy était sauvée sur la ligne (20e) puis celle de Cambot repoussée par la gardienne niçoise (38e).Avec leur petit avantage; les Vertes continuaient de monopoliser le ballon en deuxième période sans parvenir à tuer le suspense. Ninon Blanchard trouvait notamment la transversale sur corner (65e) puis Dona Scannapieco butait à son tour sur l'excellente portière azuréenne (75e). Malgré quelques timides velléités niçoises en fin de rencontre, la défense stéphanoise tenait bon pour préserver ce court mais précieux avantage.

Yannick Chandioux: "Je suis satisfait de cette victoire, notamment de notre première période, durant laquelle nous nous sommes procuré beaucoup d’occasions (...) En revanche, il n’est pas normal de ne pas avoir réussi à creuser l’écart avec une vingtaine d’occasions et plus d’une dizaine de corners. Nous avons encore du travail à faire dans ce domaine. Il faut forcément souligner cette série de six victoires consécutives en championnat. Nous avons également signé un nouveau clean-sheet, tout en nous montrant dangereux offensivement. Cette série doit surtout nous rappeler que nous devons rester pleinement concernés. J’essaie d’impliquer l’ensemble de mon groupe dans cette dynamique: chacune a eu et aura sa chance"

En effet, avec désormais 20 points au compteur, six victoires consécutives et toujours aucune défaite après huit journées, les Vertes confirment leur place de leader, uniquement talonnées par Le Mans et Roubaix, formations toutes deux victorieuses le lendemain. De quoi aborder la suite avec confiance, à commencer par un déplacement à Guéret, pensionnaire de Régional 2, dimanche prochain pour leur entrée en lice en Coupe de France. L'occasion pour les Stéphanoises de poursuivre leur belle dynamique et, pourquoi pas, de s'offrir un joli parcours dans la compétition !

Comme au match aller, il y a 4 jours, Mamour N'Diaye a assisté au match depuis le banc, sans faire d'effort certes, mais pas sans transpirer puisqu'il faisait 35 degrés à Juba, lieu du match.

Il peut donc rentrer à Sainté, où il fera 20 degrés de moins au bas mot.

#2360. Ajax, NEC and Twente win in Europe as AZ lose to Juventus

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Three of the four Dutch clubs playing in Europe on Thursday night won. Only AZ Alkmaar lost its match.

AZ lost 2-1 at home to Juventus in the Europa League.

NEC Nijmegen beat Omonia Nicosia 3-1, also in the Europa League. The Cypriot champions scored first, but NEC scored twice to make their first home win since August.

In the Conference League, Ajax thrashed Midtjylland 6-1 in Denmark.

FC Twente beat Pafos FC 3-1 in Enschede. They have now won all three of their games in the competition.

#2358. Denis Bouanga proche du triplé

Ce week-end avait lieu la suite de la phase de groupes pour la qualification à la CAN 2027 qui sera organisée par le Kenya, l'Ouganda et la Tanzanie.

Le Gabon de l'ancien Vert Denis Bouanga recevait le Lesotho. Les Panthères gabonaises l'ont emporté sur le score de 2 à 0. Deux buts inscrits par Denis Bouanga, qui aurait même pu faire un triplé. Alors que le score était encore de 0-0, il a manqué un penalty à la 64ème, juste avant de se rattraper et d'ouvrir la marque à la 65ème, pour enfin enfoncer le clou à la 79ème minute. C'était la 56ème sélection de Denis Bouanga, qui, avec ces deux buts, porte son total à 20.

Rappelons qu'il y a deux qualifiés dans chaque groupe. Après 3 matchs joués, dans le groupe A, le Maroc, avec 3 victoires est en tête, devant le Gabon (2 victoires, 1 défaite), le Niger (1 victoire, 2 défaites) et le Lesotho (3 défaites).

#2357. Candreva elogia la Lazio: "Merita di stare lassù, grande entusiasmo e sacrificio"

Candreva incorona i biancocelesti e analizza il campionato: ecco cosa ha detto sulle protagoniste.

Durante il torneo FIP Silver Mediolanum Padel Cup di Como, dove sono scesi in campo insieme ex campioni come Marco Borriello, Alessandro Budel, Enrico Annoni, Nicola Amoruso l'ex centrocampista biancoceleste Antonio Candreva ha analizzato il momento del calcio italiano, soffermandosi sulle big del campionato e celebrando lo straordinario percorso della Lazio.

CLICCA QUI E SEGUI LAZIOPRESS.IT ANCHE SU INSTAGRAM

Penso che fosse giusto ripartire con questi risultati, che hanno portato entusiasmo e aria nuova. Fin dalle prime uscite abbiamo visto una Nazionale molto bella, con entusiasmo, giocatori che si aiutano e un bel gruppo che sta nascendo.

Innanzitutto è importante per la Nazionale, dove sta facendo molto bene. È un ragazzo giovane e già determinante e secondo me ha ancora tanti margini di miglioramento. Nell'Inter ha davanti due mostri sacri come Lautaro e Thuram, ma anche all'interno delle gerarchie ha avuto modo e spazio per mettersi in evidenza. È stato comunque decisivo anche con la maglia nerazzurra. È una squadra forte, con giocatori fortissimi. Come ho sentito dire anche dal mister Chivu e da tanti altri giocatori nelle interviste post-partita, per approccio, atteggiamento e faccia mostrati nell'ultima partita non ce n'è per nessuno.

È credibilissima. Ha dimostrato di meritare di stare lì: ha entusiasmo, voglia, sacrificio e gioca bene. Se lo merita. Adesso deve pensare a una partita alla volta, perché è una squadra che si sta divertendo e si vede. Si è trovato in una squadra perfetta per lui. Siamo ancora all'inizio della stagione, ma lo conosciamo tutti. Devono continuare così, perché hanno le armi giuste per fare un grandissimo campionato.

Siamo ancora un po' all'inizio e il campionato è lungo. Poi cominceranno tante partite infrasettimanali e bisognerà vedere come le squadre arriveranno agli appuntamenti decisivi. Non contano soltanto gli scontri diretti, ma anche le partite che sulla carta possono sembrare facili e il modo in cui vengono affrontate. Bisognerà aspettare febbraio o marzo per delineare un po' meglio chi lotterà per il titolo. Lo abbiamo visto tutti: è una squadra bella da vedere, che su tutti i campi gioca con una propria identità. È un Como che darà fastidio a tutti, perché ha giocatori di qualità e un allenatore forte. Può dire la sua anche in campionato.

#2356. PSV back on top of Eredivisie as Feyenoord slump in Heerenveen

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

PSV returned to the top of the Eredivisie with a thumping 5-2 win over Cambuur Leeuwarden as previous leaders Feyenoord lost a seven-goal thriller against the other Frisian club, Heerenveen.

It took just 46 seconds for PSV to get off the mark as Sven Mijnans headed in unmarked.

The midfielder added a second after 15 minutes and completed his hat-trick with a free-kick in the 80th minute to make the score 4-2, just as Cambuur were threatening a comeback.

Feyenoord’s dip in form continued as they let a two-goal lead slip at Heerenveen. The Rotterdammers looked to be in control going into the break with a trademark drilled shot by Anis Hadj Moussa and a penalty by Nacho Ferri.

But Maas Willemsen bundled in the ball from a corner on the stroke of half-time, before Ringo Meerveld came on for the second half and scored a hat-trick as Feyenoord’s defence crumbled under pressure.

“In the matches when we played well I saw a team that fought for each other,” Feyenoord coach Giovanni van Bronckhorst said after the game. “Mentally strong, kept running even when we didn’t have the ball. That’s our strength. When we don’t do that we’re a lesser team.”

Mexx Meerdink scored a hotly contested late penalty to settle a tempestuous game in Alkmaar as AZ came back from 3-1 down against Groningen to claim their first win in five matches.

Goalkeeper Etienne Vaessen was given a second yellow card for protesting too hard against the decision to penalise him for upending Ayoub Oufkir. Once the commotion died down Meerdink, who had missed from the spot against Vaessen earlier in the second half, made no mistake against substitute goalkeeper Lovro Stubljar.

Ajax missed the chance to take over top spot at Twente as their former striker Wout Weghorst scored a last-minute penalty to rescue a point for the home side.

Ajax had been 2-0 up with a bullet header by their giant striker Tolu Arokodare and a long-range strike by Rayane Bounida, before an own goal by Dies Janse brought the visitors back into the game.

Fortuna Sittard also had to settle for a point against Telstar after going 2-0 up thanks to a bizarre own goal by Sem Valk. The defender’s sliced clearance looped over the head of Ronald Koeman Junior as the goalkeeper tried to head it away rather than risk being penalised for handling a backpass.

Goals just before half-time by Abdelnour Soualhia and Patrick Brouwer brought Telstar back into the game, but neither side was able to find a winner after the break.

That result allowed ADO, under the guidance of interim coach Levi Schwiebbe, to close the gap on 16th-placed Telstar to one point with a 3-1 win against Sparta, while bottom Willem II collected their third point of the season at home to PEC Zwolle.

#2354. Lazio, Zaccagni può tornare col Torino: Tavares verso nuovi controlli

Lunedì gli esami chiariranno le condizioni del capitano e del laterale, che ha proseguito le cure in Portogallo.

Mattia Zaccagni e Nuno Tavares saranno sottoposti a nuovi controlli lunedì. La Lazio attende gli esiti per valutare le condizioni dei due giocatori e avere indicazioni più precise sui tempi di rientro. Gli accertamenti serviranno a chiarire l’evoluzione dei problemi muscolari accusati nelle ultime settimane.

CLICCA QUI E SEGUI LAZIOPRESS.IT ANCHE SU INSTAGRAM

La visita è un appuntamento importante per lo staff biancoceleste, che dovrà stabilire quando i due calciatori potranno tornare a disposizione. Le rispettive situazioni sono diverse: per Zaccagni si guarda già alla partita contro il Torino, mentre per Tavares sarà necessario valutare a che punto sia il percorso di recupero.

Le risposte degli esami offriranno un quadro aggiornato anche per la gestione dei prossimi impegni. La Lazio spera di riavere entrambi nel minor tempo possibile, evitando però rischi di ricadute che potrebbero compromettere ulteriormente la loro stagione.

Per Zaccagni i controlli dovranno chiarire le conseguenze del problema accusato nella sfida contro il Cagliari. In un primo momento si era temuto uno stiramento, ipotesi che aveva alimentato la preoccupazione per il recupero del capitano laziale.

Ora le sensazioni sembrerebbero più incoraggianti. L’obiettivo è recuperare l’attaccante in tempo per il Torino, con la possibilità di inserirlo nell’elenco dei convocati. Il rientro, tuttavia, dipenderà dall’esito degli accertamenti e dalle successive valutazioni dello staff medico: la prospettiva resta dunque legata alle risposte attese lunedì.

#2352. Gladbach rule out winter sale of 17-year-old Bayern, Leverkusen, Brighton and Liverpool target

Wael Mohya will remain at Borussia Mönchengladbach for the rest of the season at least, sporting director Rouven Schröder has confirmed.

The 17-year-old has attracted interest from several top clubs, with Bayern Munich, Bayer Leverkusen, Brighton & Hove Albion and Liverpool reportedly among those monitoring his progress.

However, Gladbach have no intention of selling their prized asset midway through the season.

“A sale this winter is completely out of the question,” Schröder told Bild.

The sporting director also insisted that even a €50 million offer from Bayern Munich in January wouldn't change the club's stance.

“That won't happen. He is staying at Borussia; we are absolutely clear about that.”

Gladbach are reportedly working on extending Mohya's contract, which currently runs until 2028, in a bid to fend off interest from potential suitors and strengthen their negotiating position ahead of a potential future sale.

Mohya recently received his first senior Germany call-up, but was left out of the matchday squads for both the 3-1 win over Serbia and the 5-0 victory over the Netherlands.

His omission was purely down to squad restrictions, with Klopp permitted to select only 23 of the 24 called-up players for each game.

#2347. Johan Cruyff’s grandson called up to play for USA under-18 team

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

The most famous name in Dutch football could appear on an international men’s team sheet for the first time in 30 years after Johan Cruyff’s grandson was called up for the United States’ upcoming matches in Europe.

Shae Cruijff-Beane, the son of Johan Cruyff’s daughter Chantal and her American husband Todd Beane, was included in the squad that will play against Norway and Portugal in the next seven days.

Cruijff-Beane plays as a midfielder for Gimnàstic de Tarragona, a club in the Spanish third tier based near Barcelona. His older brother Jordan also came through the club’s ranks and is currently playing US college football at Westmont College in California.

Shae, 17, is eligible to play for the USA through his father and Spain and the Netherlands through his mother, who spent part of her childhood in Catalonia while Johan Cruyff was playing for Barcelona in the 1970s.

The USA under-18 squad also includes an Ajax player, midfielder Xander Newstead, who grew up in San Francisco and joined the Amsterdam club’s youth team set-up at the age of 10, beforec signing professional terms last year.

Johan Cruyff went on to play in the United States for Los Angeles Aztecs and Washington Diplomats before returning to the Netherlands, winding down his career at Ajax and Feyenoord.

His son Jordi played for Barcelona and Manchester United and won nine international caps in 1996. Last year he was appointed technical director at Ajax, the club where his father began his career.

#2345. Pandev esalta Gattuso: "Merita il primo posto, è stato l'unico a vedere le qualità della rosa"

Le parole dell'ex attaccante macedone sul momento dei biancocelesti.

Goran Pandev, ex attaccante della Lazio con cui ha vinto una Coppa Italia e una Supercoppa Italiana, ha commentato l'attuale stagione dei biancocelesti in un'intervista rilasciata all'edizione romana del Corriere della Sera, analizzando l'operato di Gennaro Gattuso, il mercato, i singoli e le ambizioni in classifica.

CLICCA QUI E SEGUI LAZIOPRESS.IT ANCHE SU INSTAGRAM

Perché Gattuso parla di quota 40 punti? Per scaramanzia. Vede i ragazzi tutti i giorni, conosce la qualità. Sapeva pure cosa aspettarsi dai giocatori che ha chiesto come Davide Frattesi e Andrea Pinamonti, che in doppia cifra ci arriva sempre. Ma Rino ha rilanciato pure Noslin, Nuno Tavares e Noslin, che solo ora stanno rendendo. I nuovi, inoltre, hanno portato voglia di vincere. Si vede che remano tutti nella stessa direzione. Il più grande merito dell'estate è stato prendere Gattuso, è stato sfortunato nella carriera da allenatore, ma è bravissimo. Le sue squadre giocano sempre bene, lui è molto intelligente, oltre a essere navigato, è un esperto di calcio. Forse è stato l'unico a vedere le qualità della squadra. Si merita il primo posto, mi auguro che lui e la Lazio possano fare bene: questa è una piazza importante ed è giusto che la squadra sia protagonista.

La Lazio veniva dipinta come scarsa, ma il livello è alto. In estate dicevano tutti che la società sarebbe stata in difficoltà perché con pochi soldi a disposizione, si parlava della proteste dei tifosi... Nessuno diceva che è stato fatto un ottimo mercato.

Una volta che si è deciso di puntare su Pinamonti era giusto andare avanti con lui. Con Gattuso può esplodere. Deve solo avere pazienza.

Mi sorprendono. Il primo anno di Claudio Lotito c'ero io: lui ha sempre avuto tensioni con i tifosi, ma portarli avanti tutti questi anni... Spero che i tifosi tornino e che si trovi un accordo. Ma non è facile. L'Olimpico vuoto è triste, specie pensando all'apporto che può dare quella gente. La Lazio Lotterà per la Champions League. Deve ancora affrontare Como, Roma e Inter, ma la Lazio è forte. E non giocare una volta ogni tre giorni aiuta.

Netherlands U21’s have one foot in the European Championships after a 3-0 win in Denmark in the first leg of their playoff.

After finishing second in their group, the Netherlands need to overcome Denmark in a two-legged playoff to seal their spot in the Euros.

Michael Reiziger handed debuts to Aaron Bouwman and Don-Angelo Konadu, while Kees Smit was not fit enough to take part.

Two own goals from Tobias Storm and Lucas Høgsberg handed the Netherlands an early 2-0 lead and just before half time, Thom van Bergen added a third.

In the second half, the Netherlands eased to victory and they will now look to seal the win on Tuesday in the Netherlands.

#2342. L'ASSE va inspirer Cédric Rullier

Alors que bon nombre d'observateurs et de spectateurs ont considéré plutôt insipide la prestation de l'ASSE hier, en Coupe de France, contre le GFA Rumilly Vallières, alors que Ian Cathro lui-même concède qu'il ne va pas très longtemps penser à ce match, Cédric Rullier, le coach des Hauts-Savoyards considère, sur le site officiel du GFA, que, dans le contenu de cette rencontre, les Stéphanois ont montré des choses dont il va pouvoir s'inspirer :

« Je tiens à remercier le FC Annecy dans son ensemble – dirigeants, staff, joueurs – qui nous a beaucoup aidé dans l’organisation, qui nous a laissé aussi l’intimité de son vestiaire. Peu de clubs l’auraient fait. Nous avions bien étudié l’ASSE et son projet de jeu vraiment très intéressant. Bravo au coach adverse d’ailleurs pour ça. Il y a des choses dont on peut s’inspirer. Sur le scénario du match, je dirais qu’on a été solides durant la première mi-temps avant de prendre le jeu à notre compte en début de seconde période, avec plusieurs occasions nettes, dont un but. D’habitude, on a un peu plus de réussite, et je pense que le match se joue là. Avec deux buts d’avance, l’issue aurait sûrement été différente. Bien sûr, il y a ce fait de jeu avec cette égalisation concédée à un de moins. Enfin, le fait d’avoir joué quatre jours avant s’est ressenti. Mais quoi qu’il arrive, je suis fier de la prestation des gars, face au meilleur club de Ligue 2. Maintenant, il faut basculer sur le championnat. Comme je l’ai toujours dit, la coupe, c’est éphémère. On a bien profité de ce bon moment et on va en tirer les enseignements. »

The Netherlands were in excellent form on Friday as they hammered Greece 7-0 to all but seal their spot in the Nations League Quarter-finals.

Xavi had Frenkie de Jong back in the midfield as he partnered Joey Veerman in midfield. Jurrien Timber played left-back as Micky van de Ven replaced the missing Virgil van Dijk. Up front, Donyell Malen led the line.

The first half was a joy to behold for Oranje fans as Netherlands ran rampant with five goals. Crysencio Summerville got the party started with a fine finish in the sixth minute. Veerman then sent an excellent through ball for Tijjani Reijnders to make it 2-0.

The Netherlands were playing lovely football with Veerman, Timber and Malen all involved. It was quickly 3-0 as Reijnders tapped in before the midfielder completed his hattrick in the 33rd minute. Before the break, Timber added the fifth.

In the second half, Teun Koopmeiners replaced De Jong but the Netherlands kept pushing forward and Timber got his second to make it 6-0. Malen then got amongst the goals for the seventh on the hour mark.

Xavi then rang more changes with Ruben van Bommel, Noa Lang, Gjivai Zechiel and Ian Maatsen all coming on. The changes took away some of the momentum and there was no further goals before the end.

The Netherlands are now almost guaranteed a place in the quarter-finals and only a huge loss to Germany on Monday would prevent this.

A wonderful evening for the Netherlands.7-0 winners over Greece!Reijnders, Veerman, Malen, Timber and Summerville all excellent.

The Netherlands are into the Quarter-finals of the Nations League but they were on the end of a poor 5-0 loss in Germany.

Following on from the 7-0 win over Greece, Netherlands headed to Germany without Frenkie de Jong. Xavi put Quinten Timber into the starting eleven.

Germany needed the win and they dominated possession from the start without ever really troubling Bart Verbruggen. The first two big chances fell to the Netherlands with Crysencio Summerville falling over when in a shooting position before Donyell Malen headed over.

Derry Scherhant hit the post for the hosts before the winger put his side ahead in the 40th minute. He was allowed to step inside before curing the ball into the top corner.

After the break, Germany continued their dominance and Florian Wirtz made it 2-0 with a fine finish on the hour. Five minutes later, Nico Schlotterbeck headed in a third.

Germany kept coming forward and Wirtz got his second with a close range finish in the 72nd minute. Gruda then added a fifth as Oranje’s players seemed to give up on defending. The players decided to have a huddle in the middle of the park with an irate Bart Verbruggen barking at his teammates.

There were no further goals but the sting of this defeat will hurt for a while. The Netherlands progress from the group but must improve hugely in the next round.

#2339. Klopp admits he was “shocked” by Wirtz after seeing Liverpool star up close

Germany head coach Jürgen Klopp has admitted he was “shocked” by Florian Wirtz's quality after watching the Liverpool star in person for the first time.

The 59-year-old spoke highly of Wirtz following Monday's 5-0 win over the Netherlands in the 2026/27 UEFA Nations League, in which the 23-year-old scored twice.

“I only knew him from watching him on television. I was shocked when I first saw him on the pitch. An extraordinary footballer,” Klopp said at the post-match press conference.

Wirtz has been in excellent form for Germany since Klopp took charge, scoring four goals in five UEFA Nations League appearances.

Klopp explained that finding the right position for the 23-year-old has helped bring out the best in him, while highlighting that his contribution goes beyond his technical ability on the ball.

“It helps that he is so vocal. He is the first player in the press and can press two players without getting tired,” Klopp added.

#2337. Dutch progress in Nations League despite 5-0 drubbing in Germany

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

The Netherlands came crashing down to earth after hammering Greece as they were outclassed and outmuscled by Germany in Berlin.

Oranje went into the final match of the Nations League group stage with high hopes of recording their first win over their old rivals in seven matches stretching back to 2019.

Instead they suffered their second worst defeat ever at the hands of Germany, but still progressed to the knockout stages thanks to their thumping 7-0 win in Amsterdam on Friday.

Coach Xavi Hernandez was forced to make one change in midfield as Jurriën Timber replaced Barcelona’s Frenkie de Jong, who pulled out with an obturator muscle strain.

Germany shaded the first half and went ahead five minutes before the break when Freiburg striker Derry Scherhant cut in from the left hand side and beat Bart Verbruggen with a curling strike into the top corner.

Scherhant had struck the post minutes earlier, while the Dutch might have taken the lead earlier when Crysencio Summerville slipped in the penalty area as he tried to control a cross by Cody Gakpo.

But in the second half the Dutch fell apart. In the 60th minute Florian Wirtz shoved Denzel Dumfries off the ball and had space to tee up a left-footed shot from the edge of the area that gave Verbruggen no chance.

Nico Schlotterbeck added a third from a free-kick five minutes later, before Wirtz drifted past Gakpo on the right side of the penalty area to score his second.

The humiliation was complete when Brajan Gruda capped a fine attacking performance by firing in a rebound.

Dumfries made no excuses afterwards for what he admitted was a “terrible performance”. “We gave the ball away too easily, left too much space and were too weak in the challenges,” he told NOS. “We can’t let that happen.”

#2333. Klopp reveals he wanted to bring Germany star to Liverpool

After taking over as Germany coach, Jürgen Klopp made Marc-André ter Stegen his first-choice goalkeeper.

Speaking to ARD on Monday, Klopp revealed that he has long been an admirer of the 34-year-old, who is currently on loan at Ajax from Barcelona.

In fact, the former Liverpool manager had previously tried to bring the German shot-stopper to Anfield during his time on Merseyside.

“I have always considered him an exceptional goalkeeper and wanted to bring him to Liverpool in the past,” Klopp said.

Ter Stegen ultimately opted to remain at Barcelona, but Klopp insists there are no hard feelings.

“I'm not one to hold a grudge,” the Germany head coach added with a smile.

#2332. On a déconné avec Da Cunha (22)

Resté un grand supporter des Verts qui l'ont pourtant recalé plusieurs fois à l'adolescence au grand dam de Dominique Rocheteau, Lucas Da Cunha est "le grand gagnant de l'ère Zidane" comme l'a indiqué aujourd'hui Le Dauphiné Libéré.

L'AFP souligne les performances du natif de Roanne (Loire) en équipe de France, jugées "très satisfaisantes" par son sélectionneur. "L'ailier de formation a été placé en meneur de jeu par Cesc Fabregas en Serie A où il s'est révélé après quelques échecs en Ligue 1. Le patron des Bleus l'a encore fait reculer d'un cran en le plaçant dans un rôle de sentinelle où Da Cunha, qui découvrait le poste, a montré beaucoup de promesses et quelques lacunes, en défense notamment. Mais Zidane qui a procédé à une large revue d'effectif lors des deux rassemblements de l'automne, lui a accordé une confiance telle que le capitaine de Côme est le joueur de champ qui compte le plus de temps de jeu à égalité avec Michael Olise (386 minutes chacun)."

Dans sa dernière édition, la Pravda n'est pas en reste. "On dit d'un entraîneur qu'il couche toujours un nom en premier quand il compose son onze de départ. Concernant Zinédine Zidane chez les Bleus, on va finir par penser que ce nom est celui de Lucas Da Cunha, qui avait été le meilleur Français lors de la défaite en ltalie. Contre la Turquie, le meneur de jeu reculé a cherché à accélérer la circulation de balle des Bleus, qui manquait souvent de verticalité, tout en grattant plusieurs ballons au pressing ou grâce à ses anticipations (7 récupérations, record du match côté français). Depuis sa position basse, il est capable de renverser le jeu pour donner de l'air à l'équipe, mais aussi d'offrir de très bons ballons de but, comme il l'a fait deux fois pour Kylian Mbappé en dépassant son poste de sentinelle."

"Déjà un pilier de l'ère Zidane" dixit Le Parisien, le joueur de 25 ans savoure sur TF1. "Les compliments de Zidane sont géniaux, c’est exceptionnel. Il m’a donné beaucoup de responsabilités depuis que je suis arrivé. J’essaie d’appliquer tout ce qu’il me demande, que ce soit sur le plan défensif ou offensif. Je sens que j'ai encore une grosse marge de progression, c'est ça qui est super intéressant pour moi. C’est sûr que l’ascension est folle. Il y a encore quelques années, j’étais ailier. Aujourd’hui, je suis milieu de terrain et je suis là avec les Bleus. Quand on commence le foot, quand on est jeune, c’est un rêve de pouvoir porter ce maillot. On rêve de ça. Et le jour où ça arrive, on n’y croit pas trop. J’adore, j’y prends goût. C’est une grande fierté d’être ici."

#2331. Lotito sulla Reggina: «non sono soldi che provengono dalla Lazio»

Il club amaranto è posseduto dal figlio; Lotito distingue le due proprietà e chiede di cambiare le norme sulla multiproprietà.

Claudio Lotito afferma che la Reggina è di suo figlio, che ha scelto di investire nel club, e che la proprietà amaranto è distinta da quella della Lazio. Secondo quanto riportato da Seried24, Le parole arrivano dopo il 3-2 sul Sambiase nello scontro diretto per la vetta: la Reggina è ora sola al primo posto nel girone.

CLICCA QUI E SEGUI LAZIOPRESS.IT ANCHE SU INSTAGRAM

Nella conferenza stampa al termine della partita, riportata da Seried24, Lotito ha affrontato anche la propria ricandidatura a consigliere federale, il progetto a Reggio Calabria e il tema delle strutture.

Parlando delle elezioni, Lotito ha collegato la scelta di rimettersi in gioco alla propria esperienza e alla necessità di riformare il calcio: «Ho lavorato per tanti anni come consigliere federale e consigliere di Lega, cercando sempre di contribuire alla crescita del sistema calcio. Ho deciso di rimettermi in gioco perché ritengo necessario un percorso di riforme che renda il calcio italiano più moderno, sia dal punto di vista organizzativo che normativo. Esistono ancora regole che non rispondono più alle esigenze attuali di un settore che ha assunto un’importanza economica notevole. Bisogna avere una visione e costruire qualcosa che possa durare nel tempo».

Lotito ha poi chiarito le ragioni della sua scelta: «Ho deciso di ricandidarmi come consigliere federale non per una questione personale, ma per mettere a disposizione l’esperienza maturata in questi anni. Ho contribuito a diverse riforme, anche sul piano economico e normativo, e credo che il sistema abbia ancora bisogno di cambiamenti importanti. L’obiettivo è lavorare nei prossimi due anni per rendere il calcio italiano più moderno, sostenibile e organizzato».

Sull’impegno a Reggio Calabria, Lotito ha escluso che si tratti di un’esperienza temporanea: «Non sono arrivato a Reggio Calabria per caso e non considero questa esperienza una parentesi. Ho scelto di impegnarmi in questo progetto perché credo di poter contribuire a risolvere determinati problemi».

Ha quindi parlato del rapporto con il sindaco Cannizzaro e delle proprie origini: «Con il sindaco Cannizzaro condividiamo un’affinità caratteriale e la volontà di lavorare concretamente per il territorio. Ho anche origini calabresi da parte di mio padre e conosco l’importanza che qui assumono valori come dignità, orgoglio e senso di appartenenza».

Quanto al Sant’Agata, Lotito ha legato il lavoro sulle strutture alla prospettiva politica e sportiva della città: «Ancora è prematuro, lavoriamo in sinergia con l'amministrazione sulle strutture. Si apre una stagione nuova in termini politici e sportivi, Reggio è un territorio abbandonato dalla politica da tanto tempo».

#2328. « Je suis candidat à l'élection présidentielle de 2027 » : L'annonce inattendue de Teddy Riner !

C'est une annonce pour le moins inattendue dans le monde du sport tricolore. Ce lundi 9 novembre 2026, Teddy Riner a officialisé sa candidature à l'élection présidentielle de 2027 dans une vidéo publiée sur son compte X, tout en lançant son propre mouvement politique intitulé « La France qu'on veut ».

Le judoka français de 37 ans se lance ainsi en politique après avoir dominé le judo international. Quintuple champion olympique et onze fois champion du monde, Teddy Riner a bâti un palmarès exceptionnel qui le place au sommet de sa discipline. Alors que son avenir sportif restait au cœur des discussions depuis les Jeux de Paris, le Français surprend en ouvrant un tout autre chapitre personnel. Un virage spectaculaire.

Dans une vidéo publiée ce lundi 9 novembre 2026 sur son compte X, Teddy Riner a pris la parole face caméra afin de lever le voile sur ses intentions pour la prochaine présidentielle. Le judoka de 37 ans a officialisé sa démarche avec des mots simples et directs.

Conscient des réactions que son entrée en politique peut susciter, le quintuple champion olympique a tenu à devancer immédiatement les critiques concernant son manque d'expérience dans les fonctions publiques. Teddy Riner a ainsi déclaré : « Je sais ce qu'on va dire de moi. Il est fou, il n'est pas du sérail, il n'a pas les codes, il n'a jamais fait de politique. Mais posez-vous la question avec moi, qu'est-ce qui est fou aujourd'hui ? Je n'ai pas passé ma vie derrière un public, mais le combat a toujours fait partie de moi. » Une détermination affichée.

Pour concrétiser ses ambitions, le judoka français de 37 ans a également fondé sa propre formation politique ce lundi 9 novembre 2026, baptisée « La France qu'on veut ». Cette prise de parole sur les réseaux sociaux a d'ailleurs été accompagnée d'un entretien accordé au quotidien Le Parisien pour préciser le sens de sa démarche. Dans cet échange, Teddy Riner revendique une volonté de rassemblement sans affiliation partisane, affirmant vouloir devenir un « président qui fédère » sans se situer à droite ou à gauche.

En effet, le champion tricolore a expliqué que sa décision avait mûri dans le sillage direct de l'élan collectif suscité par les Jeux olympiques de Paris 2024. Porté par cette dynamique populaire, il entend désormais transposer cette ferveur sur le plan politique. Ainsi, son mouvement politique refuse d'entrer dans les clivages traditionnels pour privilégier une adhésion commune à l'échelle du pays. Un projet ambitieux.

Toutefois, cette ambition politique ne pousse pas Teddy Riner vers la retraite sportive. Sur le plan des compétitions, sa dernière apparition individuelle remonte aux Jeux olympiques de Paris en août 2024, suivie d'une participation sous les couleurs du PSG Judo en Ligue des champions en décembre 2024. Malgré cette nouvelle démarche politique, le quintuple champion olympique et onze fois champion du monde de judo demeure bel et bien un athlète en activité.

Au-delà de l'élection présidentielle de 2027, Teddy Riner a ainsi fait part de son souhait de participer aux Jeux olympiques de Los Angeles 2028 si ses futures responsabilités et les Français le lui permettent. Le judoka français lie donc son avenir sportif à la suite de son engagement public, avec en ligne de mire les Jeux olympiques de Los Angeles 2028.

Mercato - Ça bouge à l’OM : Qui doit être le prochain joueur à partir cet été ?
